subject: Strategic renewal exception request — Quantix (tiered credits + SLO addendum)
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@quantix.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lara Ortiz <lara.ortiz@quantix.ai>, Procurement <procurement@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion & ask — Quantix renewal (Dec 1)

Diego,

We're preparing for our Dec 1 renewal and need to align quickly. Usage for our non-core workloads dropped ~37% year-over-year and several production incidents over the summer (latency spikes on the inference API) have our finance and engineering teams requesting concessions to proceed.

What we're asking for:
- A one-time credit applied to annual invoice reflecting the drop in consumption (Quantix is seeking ~20% off committed spend)
- Reset the committed term to 12 months (rather than 24) to match our roadmap
- A short SLO addendum (99.9% API availability) for 6 months with a documented escalation path

I've attached our usage report and a short incident timeline. If we can land near these terms we'd be able to sign on Dec 1. Can you confirm what flexibility Redwood can offer and next steps?

Thanks,
Alex Chen\Head of Infrastructure\Quantix.ai

Attachments: Usage_Report_Q1-Q3.csv (csv) ; Incident_Summary_Sep-Oct.pdf (pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@quantix.ai>
Cc: Lara Ortiz <lara.ortiz@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion & ask — Quantix renewal (Dec 1)

Alex — appreciate the context and the timeline.

High level: we want to keep Quantix on the platform (strategic account) and understand the impact of the incidents. I can put together a one-off package for this renewal, but I need approvals from pricing and my exec for anything beyond the standard concessions.

Prelim we can consider:
- One-time credit on the next invoice (range: 10–15% pending approval)
- Shorter term (12 months) is feasible operationally — need procurement language
- We can propose an SLO addendum for 6 months, contingent on SRE sign-off and a capped remediation credit structure (not open-ended refunds)

I'll escalate internally today and follow up with a concrete proposal and impact on ARR. Can you share any specific procurement timelines and which legal signatory will handle DocuSign?

Best,
Diego Fernandez\Senior Account Executive, Renewals\Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Quantix renewal — request for exception authority

Team — looping you in with the customer's ask (see attached usage + incident summary). Key points and recommended package to close by 2026-12-01: 

Proposed one-off package (customer-facing):
- One-time credit = 15% of committed annual invoice (applied to next invoice)
- Term reset to 12 months (from proposed 24) with standard opt-out language on non-payment
- 6-month SLO addendum: 99.9% availability target for API endpoints, with a capped service credit policy (max 5% of monthly invoice for breach) and a documented escalation timetable to Redwood SRE + CS
- No changes to data residency or privacy terms

Rationale: Strategic relationship, multi-product expansion potential next year, and risk of churn if we don't offer a meaningful concession. Impact: ~ -15% on committed ARR for year one (~$360k credit) but preserves renewal and upsell runway.

Ask: Priyom — can Legal/Deal Desk draft redlined language for the SLO addendum and procurement? Marissa — can you weigh in on account health and whether CS can commit to the SRE escalation cadence? Vivek — this exceeds standard delegated discount authority; please advise if you can approve the 15% credit + 6-month SLO addendum.

Attachments: Quantix_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf; Usage_Report_Q1-Q3.csv; Quantix_Risk_Assessment.pdf

Thanks,
Diego

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Quantix renewal — request for exception authority

Diego/Marissa — reviewed the package and legal implications. Quick notes: 

- Pricing/credits: Deal Desk can approve up to 12% one-time credit under delegated authority for renewals. Anything above 12% requires VP (Vivek) sign-off. Please quantify the revenue delta precisely (I see Diego's $360k figure; confirm committed ARR baseline).
- SLO addendum: Legal will need a tightly-scoped addendum. Engineering/SRE must sign off on the SLO target and the remediation credit cap. Our preference is to limit SLO addenda to 3 months for first-time exceptions unless we get formal SRE assurances. A 6-month duration is possible but requires an SRE runbook and a sunset clause.
- Term reset: Operationally OK, but procurement should accept renewal pricing floor language. We should require a clause preventing multiple consecutive resets.

Next steps I propose: Priyom -> I'll draft the redline for the SLO addendum (tracked change) and a procurement memo. Diego, please confirm the committed ARR number and the customer's procurement signatory — we need that for formal approval routing. Vivek — tagging you for sign-off if Diego wants to push to 15%/6 months.

--
Priyom Das\Senior Counsel, Deal Desk\Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Quantix renewal — request for exception authority

Diego / team — after reviewing the context and upstream risk, I'm comfortable approving a constrained exception to preserve this strategic relationship. Approvals granted with these firm conditions: 

1) One-time credit — approve 15% of the committed annual invoice (applied to next invoice). This is the final approved concession; no further credits to be given without additional exec review.
2) Term reset — approve to 12 months but include a single-use clause: term reset may not be requested again at next renewal cycle.
3) SLO addendum — approve a 6-month SLO at 99.9% availability with a capped remediation credit (max 5% of monthly invoice). Prior to signing, SRE must provide the runbook and confirm feasibility.
4) Legal & Procurement deliverables: Priyom to provide redline; Diego to obtain customer's procurement signatory and execute via DocuSign. Quantix must sign the SLO addendum and procurement memo before credits are posted.

Diego — you have authorization to proceed on these terms. Please update HubSpot (deal QX-2026-RWL-42) and coordinate with CS to schedule the SRE runbook review. Once executed, Finance will apply the one-time credit to the upcoming invoice.

Vivek Kulkarni\VP, Commercial Operations\Redwood Inference
